title: Tata's JLR Targets Double-Digit Earnings Growth in Fiscal 2028 After Guidance Cut
excerpt: Reuters reports the fiscal 2028 target rests on £1.7 billion of cost cuts and new electric models — separate from the reported September-quarter loss of £451 million and a fiscal 2027 margin outlook cut to 2% to 3%.
body:
• Jaguar Land Rover is targeting double-digit growth in core earnings in fiscal 2028, according to Reuters — a target, not a result, banking on a £1.7 billion cost-cutting drive, new electric models and North America growth.
  • What JLR actually reported for the second quarter of fiscal 2027 (July to September 2026) was revenue of £5.9 billion and a profit before tax and exceptional items of just £6 million, an adjusted EBIT margin of 1.1%; after £530 million of exceptional charges, it recorded a loss of £451 million.
  • For fiscal 2027, JLR cut its guidance: an adjusted core earnings margin of 2% to 3%, down from about 4% set in June, revenue of about £25 billion, and free cash outflow of about £1.25 billion.
  • For Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles shareholders, the test is execution: whether the cost programme lowers JLR's cash break-even to about 300,000 vehicles before the fiscal 2028 target comes due.

Jaguar Land Rover, the British luxury carmaker owned by India's Tata Motors, is targeting double-digit growth in core earnings in fiscal 2028, according to Reuters, even as it cut its guidance for the current year and reported a quarterly loss driven by restructuring charges. The three numbers in this story belong to three different periods, and they should not be blended: a reported September quarter, a lowered fiscal 2027 outlook, and a fiscal 2028 target that is guidance, not performance.

What JLR reported for the September quarter

For the second quarter of fiscal 2027, the three months to September 2026, JLR reported revenue of £5,894 million and wholesale volumes of 82,487 vehicles, according to its official results page. Profit before tax and exceptional items was £6 million, free cash flow was an outflow of £540 million, and the adjusted EBIT margin was 1.1%. The year-ago comparison is flattered by a cyber incident that had shut down production then.

Including exceptional items, the quarter looks very different. Reporting on the results put JLR's loss at £451 million after £530 million of exceptional charges, of which £295 million relates to a voluntary redundancy programme covering about 4,000 people. At the parent, Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles reported a consolidated net loss of ₹5,451 crore for the September quarter, on consolidated revenue that rose 34% to ₹96,920 crore, according to results coverage of the Tata Motors filing. Excluding a one-time demerger gain of ₹82,616 crore that inflated the year-ago profit, the prior-year quarter was a loss of ₹6,368 crore.

The guidance cut for fiscal 2027

For the full year to March 2027, JLR now expects an adjusted operating margin of 2% to 3%, down from the 4% target set in June, revenue of about £25 billion, down from about £26 billion, and a free cash outflow of about £1.25 billion, according to Reuters. The company blamed market challenges, geopolitical risks and the exceptional costs recognised in the quarter. That is a forecast about a year still in progress — not a reported result — and the September quarter's 1.1% adjusted margin shows the ground the second half must make up.

The fiscal 2028 target and the plan behind it

The fiscal 2028 ambition rests on a two-year restructuring programme targeting manufacturing, materials, logistics and warranty costs, worth £1.7 billion, intended to lower JLR's cash break-even volume to about 300,000 vehicles, Reuters reported. Of the roughly 4,000 people in the voluntary redundancy programme, chief financial officer Richard Molyneux said about 3,000 colleagues have signed up and will leave this fiscal year, most of them at the end of this month.

"Together with our growth plans for the US and disciplined execution of our enterprise missions to reduce our break-even to 300,000 units, position us well to deliver consistent cash-accretive growth in the coming years."

— PB Balaji, JLR Chief Executive, on the post-earnings call reported by Reuters

The product side of the plan is already visible. JLR said it launched three luxury electric vehicles in the quarter — Range Rover Electric, Range Rover Sport Electric and the Jaguar Type 01, premiered in New York — with a Range Rover GT and a new electric Defender product proposed for the new year. North America is the growth market management is pointing to: wholesales there rose 20% year-on-year in the first half of fiscal 2027, Reuters reported. China is the offset. JLR's Chinese volumes fell sharply in the quarter, the market there was down almost 30%, and wholesale volumes in China fell to about 6,100 vehicles from more than 11,000 a year earlier, according to the results coverage.

What to watch next

Three things will show whether the fiscal 2028 target is credible. First, the break-even programme: whether the £1.7 billion of targeted savings actually lands in the recurring cost base. Second, China and trade: management flagged geopolitical risk and tariff exposure, and chief executive PB Balaji has argued, in reporting by The Guardian, that Britain and the European Union should not add new post-Brexit trade barriers on electric cars. Third, the balance sheet: results coverage put JLR's net debt at ₹53,000 crore and consolidated net debt at ₹50,800 crore, up from ₹30,700 crore at the end of fiscal 2026, while Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles shares have fallen 22% this year.
